hook: A female cod can release millions of eggs in one spawning season and then swim away; almost all of them are eaten or die before they grow up. A female elephant carries one calf for about 22 months and then spends years protecting and teaching it. Both strategies keep their species going. They are two ends of a range of reproductive strategies called r-selected and K-selected.

prereq.q: Which kind of species can switch to other foods when its main food declines?
prereq.why: Generalists have broad niches, so they have other foods to switch to.

prereq.q: After a fire, which plants usually arrive first on the bare soil?
prereq.why: Pioneer species in secondary succession are fast-growing grasses and weeds.

figure.caption: Traits of r-selected and K-selected species. Most species fall somewhere between the two ends.

chain.cause: An r-selected species produces many small offspring early in life and gives them little care
chain.effect: most offspring die young, but the population can grow very quickly when conditions are good

chain.cause: A disruption kills much of the population
chain.effect: an r-selected species rebounds fast, because each survivor can soon produce many offspring

chain.cause: A K-selected species produces few large offspring late in life and cares for them
chain.effect: more of each offspring survive, but the population grows slowly and recovers slowly after losses

ideas: Biotic potential is the fastest rate at which a population could grow if it had unlimited resources. r-selected species have a high biotic potential; K-selected species have a low one.
r-selected species: many small offspring, little or no parental care, early first reproduction, short lives. Insects, mice, many fish and weeds.
K-selected species: few large offspring, much parental care, late first reproduction, long lives. Elephants, whales, great apes, many large trees.

K-selected populations tend to stay near the largest size their environment can support; r-selected populations swing up and down. After a disruption, r-selected species rebound quickly; K-selected species recover slowly and are more at risk of dying out.

misconception.wrong: A species is either r-selected or K-selected, nothing in between.
misconception.right: r and K are the two ends of a range. Many species are in between: sea turtles lay many eggs and give no care (r-like) but live long and start breeding late (K-like).

summary: r-selected species have many small offspring, little parental care, early reproduction and short lives; they have a high biotic potential, their populations swing up and down, and they rebound quickly after a disruption. K-selected species have few large offspring, much parental care, late reproduction and long lives; their populations are steadier but recover slowly from losses. Most species fall between the two ends.
